t: Begun by Martin Luther’s protest against the sale of indulgences in 1517, the Reformation broke the unity of Western Christianity and created Lutheran, Reformed, Anglican and Anabaptist churches.
Its teachers held that sinners are saved by God’s grace through faith alone, that scripture is the highest authority in the Church and that all believers share in one priesthood.
Taken up or resisted by princes and cities, it became bound up with politics and war, until the Peace of Westphalia of 1648 ended the wars of religion in the Holy Roman Empire.
dyk: The name Protestant comes from a protest: at the Diet of Speyer in 1529 six princes and fourteen imperial cities formally protested against the majority’s decision to restore the Edict of Worms against Luther’s teaching.
ev: Martin Luther writes his Ninety-five Theses against the sale of indulgences
Luther refuses to recant at the Diet of Worms and is outlawed by the Edict of Worms
The German Peasants’ War is crushed; the first adult baptisms in Zurich begin the Anabaptist movement
The Act of Supremacy makes Henry VIII supreme head of the Church of England
John Calvin returns to Geneva, which adopts his Ecclesiastical Ordinances
The Peace of Augsburg lets each prince of the empire choose Catholicism or Lutheranism for his lands
Henry IV of France grants the Huguenots toleration in the Edict of Nantes
The Peace of Westphalia ends the Thirty Years’ War and recognises the Reformed faith in the empire

f.where: Arose at Wittenberg in Saxony and at Zurich, then spread through the German lands and Switzerland to Scandinavia, England, Scotland, the Netherlands, France, Bohemia, Hungary and Poland-Lithuania
f.period: 1517–1648: from Luther’s Ninety-five Theses to the Peace of Westphalia; its main churches founded by the 1560s
f.figures: Martin Luther, Huldrych Zwingli, Philip Melanchthon, John Calvin, Thomas Cranmer, John Knox
f.outcome: Lasting Protestant churches beside the Catholic Church, and a Europe divided by confession, recognised in the empire by the Peace of Augsburg (1555) and the Peace of Westphalia (1648)
